meta.name: AWS SysOps Administrator Associate (SOA-C02)
meta.notes: [hardening pass: rebuilt correct-answer truncations, length-balanced distractors, removed absolute-language tells] | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass: 30 questions fixed (0% tell rate)

questions.question: A SysOps engineer configures a CloudWatch alarm to notify the operations team when EC2 CPU utilization exceeds 80% for 5 consecutive minutes. The alarm is in ALARM state and sends an SNS notification, but the on-call engineer reports they received no email. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: CloudWatch only sends one notification per alarm state transition
The EC2 instance does not have the CloudWatch agent installed, which is required to publish CPU utilization metrics
CloudWatch alarm actions support only Auto Scaling and EC2 actions for EC2 metrics, not SNS notifications
The SNS topic email subscription has not been confirmed by the recipient and is still in 'Pending Confirmation' state
questions.explanation: SNS email subscriptions require the recipient to confirm the subscription by clicking a confirmation link. Until confirmed, the subscription stays in 'Pending Confirmation' and no emails are delivered. Always verify each SNS email subscription is confirmed after setup.

questions.question: An application logs errors to CloudWatch Logs in the format 'ERROR: RequestId <id> Duration: <ms>'. The operations team wants a metric that counts the number of errors per minute to trigger an alarm. Which CloudWatch feature should the SysOps engineer use?
options: A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter that streams the log events to Kinesis Data Firehose for downstream aggregation
An EventBridge rule that triggers on a CloudWatch Logs event pattern matching the 'ERROR' string in the message body
A CloudWatch Logs metric filter that matches the 'ERROR' pattern and publishes a count to a custom namespace metric
CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that replay the failing requests on a schedule and emit a failure metric per run
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs metric filters extract numeric values or count occurrences from log events and convert them into CloudWatch metrics. You define a filter pattern (such as 'ERROR'), optionally extract a value, and specify a metric in a custom namespace. The resulting metric can drive a CloudWatch alarm.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure that all newly created S3 buckets in their AWS account have server-side encryption enabled. The SysOps team needs to be automatically notified when a non-compliant bucket is found and see compliance history over time. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the organization root that denies CreateBucket unless the bucket has server-side encryption enabled — this enforces the requirement but does not mark existing non-compliant buckets as compliant in Config

Create a Lambda function triggered by an S3 event notification that inspects bucket policies and enables default encryption if missing — reactive remediation, but does not continuously evaluate compliant state across all buckets
Enable AWS Config with the managed rule 's3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled' and route NON_COMPLIANT change events to SNS

Use CloudTrail to detect CreateBucket API calls and route the event through EventBridge to a Lambda remediation function — ensures new buckets are enabled with encryption but leaves existing non-compliant buckets unaddressed
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configurations against managed or custom rules. The 's3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled' managed rule detects non-compliant S3 buckets, Config maintains compliance history, and SNS/EventBridge notifications can fire when compliance status changes. SCPs prevent creation but do not track existing buckets.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to automatically stop an EC2 instance that has been in 'running' state for more than 24 hours without any active connections. The company wants to minimize idle compute costs. Which solution uses the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Rely on AWS Trusted Advisor to detect idle instances and have the on-call engineer review and stop them on a weekly basis
Enable EC2 instance auto-recovery and attach a CloudWatch alarm that stops the instance when its NetworkIn metric is sustained near zero
Author a Lambda function that polls EC2 DescribeInstances every hour and stops any instance whose running state exceeds 24 hours
Schedule an EventBridge cron rule that invokes a Systems Manager Automation document to evaluate idle instances and stop qualifying ones
questions.explanation: EventBridge scheduled rules invoking an SSM Automation document provide serverless, low-maintenance automation. The Automation document can check instance state and CloudWatch connection metrics and stop the qualifying instances. No EC2-hosted logic or manual review is required — the workflow runs entirely on managed AWS services.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer reviews CloudTrail and notices API calls from an unknown IP address creating IAM users with administrator privileges at 2 AM. The engineer needs to identify which AWS account credentials were used to make these calls. Which CloudTrail field contains this information?
options: sourceIPAddress
userIdentity
eventSource
requestParameters
questions.explanation: The 'userIdentity' field in CloudTrail event records identifies the requester — it includes the type (IAMUser, AssumedRole, Root), ARN, account ID, and the access key ID used. This is the field investigators examine when determining which credentials were used for an API call. sourceIPAddress shows where the call came from, not who made it.

questions.question: A company's operations team receives hundreds of CloudWatch alarms daily and is experiencing alert fatigue. Many alarms fire for brief metric spikes that self-resolve within seconds. What is the MOST effective way to reduce noise while ensuring real problems are still detected?
options: Configure the alarm to notify only during business hours by routing the SNS action through EventBridge time-based filtering
Replace the static-threshold alarm with CloudWatch Anomaly Detection so the band adjusts itself to the metric's recent history
Increase the evaluation period and the number of datapoints required to trigger (for example, 3 out of 5 evaluation periods)
Raise the alarm threshold value substantially so only extreme metric values cross the line and trigger the alarm action
questions.explanation: The 'M out of N datapoints' alarm configuration requires M datapoints within a window of N evaluation periods to breach the threshold before the alarm fires. This filters out brief transient spikes — for example, '3 out of 5' means 3 of the last five 5-minute periods must breach, significantly reducing false positives.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to query CloudWatch Logs to find the top 10 API Gateway endpoints by request count over the past 7 days. The logs are in a structured JSON format. Which tool provides this capability natively?
options: CloudWatch Logs Insights with a stats command that groups by endpoint field and sorts by count descending

Athena querying a table created from a daily CloudWatch Logs export to S3 in the past 24 hours — adds latency of up to 24 hours and requires running a separate count query per endpoint rather than a real-time stats command
AWS Glue crawlers configured to crawl CloudWatch Logs directly and expose them to ad-hoc query engines

CloudWatch Metrics Math expressions that calculate request count derived from log metric filters per endpoint — metric filters must be pre-defined per endpoint and cannot dynamically group and count arbitrary field values
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights supports an interactive query syntax such as 'stats count(*) by endpoint | sort count desc | limit 10' against any CloudWatch log group. It natively handles JSON-structured logs, automatically parses fields, and supports ad-hoc or scheduled queries. Results can be exported or added to dashboards.

questions.question: An organization manages 12 AWS accounts. The security team needs a single dashboard that shows AWS Config compliance status across all accounts and regions. Which service provides this aggregated view?
options: An AWS Config aggregator collecting configuration and compliance data from every source account and region into one view
AWS Security Hub with its aggregated findings view enabled across all member accounts in the organization
AWS Control Tower's compliance dashboard, which surfaces Config conformance status across the enrolled accounts
Cross-account CloudWatch dashboards in the AWS Organizations management account showing Config metrics per region
questions.explanation: An AWS Config aggregator collects configuration and compliance data from multiple source accounts and regions into a single AWS Config view. You can query compliance status, configuration history, and resource inventory across all accounts. This is the native AWS Config feature for multi-account compliance visibility.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer is troubleshooting intermittent connectivity failures to an EC2 instance. VPC Flow Logs are enabled. The engineer needs to determine whether traffic from a specific client IP is being rejected by the security group or NACL. What should the engineer look for in VPC Flow Logs?
options: Flow logs records with a REJECT action from the ENI, indicating that either the security group or NACL denied the traffic — flow logs do record REJECTs but cannot identify whether the security-group logs or NACL logs caused the rejection
Flow logs cannot distinguish security-group from NACL denials — both surface as REJECT — use VPC Reachability Analyzer instead
Flow logs records emitted from the security group itself with action REJECT and the specific security group rule ID
Flow logs records with a DROP action that surface the specific NACL rule number that denied the packet
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record ACCEPT or REJECT actions but do not indicate whether a security group or a NACL caused the rejection — both appear as REJECT. To pinpoint the blocking component, use VPC Reachability Analyzer, which evaluates the path through NACLs and security groups and identifies which component blocks the traffic.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer configures a CloudWatch alarm to trigger an EC2 auto-recovery action when the system status check fails. The engineer also wants to be notified when the recovery is initiated. How should the notification be configured?
options: Create a separate CloudWatch alarm on the 'StatusCheckFailed_System' metric with an auto-recovery action to send notifications — this adds a separate recovery alarm but does not integrate with the existing auto recovery alarm already configured
Attach an SNS notification action to the same CloudWatch alarm that already triggers the EC2 auto-recovery action

Use EventBridge to match 'EC2 Instance Recovery' events emitted by the EC2 service and route them to an SNS topic — EventBridge can detect recovery completion events but the auto recovery action itself is already on the CloudWatch alarm

Enable EC2 instance event notifications in the EC2 console under 'Events and Scheduled Changes' so the team receives auto-generated alerts — EC2 scheduled event notifications are separate from CloudWatch alarm notification actions; adding an SNS action directly to the alarm is simpler
questions.explanation: A single CloudWatch alarm can have multiple actions. You can attach both an EC2 recovery action and an SNS notification action to the same alarm. When the alarm transitions to ALARM, all configured actions execute simultaneously — the instance recovery begins and the SNS notification is sent.

questions.question: A company's application generates 10 GB of logs daily in CloudWatch Logs. After 90 days, logs are rarely accessed but must be retained for 7 years for compliance. What is the MOST cost-effective approach?
options: Set the CloudWatch log group retention to 7 years (2555 days) and leave the data in CloudWatch Logs storage
Use a Lambda function triggered by CloudWatch Events to export logs to S3 Standard storage class on a daily schedule
Export logs daily to an S3 bucket and use S3 lifecycle rules to transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days
Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights to archive old log data automatically to a low-cost tier after the 90-day window
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs storage is significantly more expensive than S3, especially compared to Glacier Deep Archive. The recommended pattern is to export logs from CloudWatch Logs to S3, then use S3 lifecycle rules to transition to cheaper tiers like Standard-IA after 30 days and Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days. CloudWatch Logs retention only deletes, it does not archive cheaply.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to detect when any AWS root account login occurs and immediately alert the security team. Which combination of services achieves this with the LEAST latency?
options: Enable CloudTrail, create an EventBridge rule that matches ConsoleLogin events where userIdentity.type is Root, and route to SNS
Enable GuardDuty, which natively detects root user sign-in events and emits a high-severity finding within minutes
Configure AWS Config with a custom rule that detects root logins by evaluating recent CloudTrail event history hourly
Schedule a Lambda function via EventBridge that runs hourly to scan CloudTrail event history for root sign-in events
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records all API and console events, including root sign-in. EventBridge matches CloudTrail events in near-real-time with event pattern filters. A rule matching ConsoleLogin events where userIdentity.type equals 'Root' fires immediately on a root login and routes the event to SNS for instant notification — typically within 15 seconds of the event.

questions.question: An Auto Scaling group is running an application tier. During deployments, new instances sometimes receive traffic before the application has fully initialized, causing user errors. What is the correct mechanism to prevent this?
options: Use CloudFormation rolling updates with a minimum-successful-instances percentage that gates traffic during deployments
Configure the EC2 health check grace period long enough that the ASG does not terminate the new instance prematurely
Increase the default cooldown period of the Auto Scaling group to allow more time between successive scale-out events
Add a lifecycle hook on autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING that holds the instance in Pending:Wait until initialization completes
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks pause instances in a wait state during launch (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING) or termination. The instance stays in 'Pending:Wait' while your initialization script runs (pull code, run health checks). Once ready, the script calls CompleteLifecycleAction so the instance proceeds to InService and begins receiving load-balancer traffic.

questions.question: A company runs a critical web application in us-east-1. They need a disaster recovery strategy with an RTO of 30 minutes and an RPO of 1 hour, at minimum additional cost. Which DR strategy best fits these requirements?
options: Pilot light: keep only the core database and AMIs warm in us-west-2 and provision the full stack on disaster
Backup and restore: take hourly snapshots and rebuild the environment from scratch during a disaster event
Warm standby: maintain a scaled-down but running copy of the stack in us-west-2 and scale up during failover
Multi-site active-active: run a full production environment in us-west-2 concurrently with us-east-1 serving traffic
questions.explanation: Warm standby keeps a reduced-capacity, fully functional copy of the environment running in the DR region. During failover, you scale up the standby (typically via ASG modifications) to handle production traffic. This achieves an RTO of minutes to ~30 minutes at significantly lower cost than active-active. Pilot light usually exceeds a 30-minute RTO due to provisioning time.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to configure Route 53 health checks so that traffic automatically fails over from the primary region to a secondary region when the primary becomes unhealthy. Which Route 53 routing policy should be used?
options: Geolocation routing with health checks configured for the primary region and a default record for the secondary
Latency-based routing with health checks attached to both records so failed targets are taken out of rotation
Failover routing with the primary record designated PRIMARY and the secondary record designated SECONDARY
Weighted routing with a weight of 100 on the primary record and a weight of 0 on the secondary record
questions.explanation: Route 53 Failover routing is purpose-built for active-passive failover. You designate one record as PRIMARY and another as SECONDARY. Route 53 routes traffic to the PRIMARY while its health check passes; when the PRIMARY health check fails, Route 53 automatically routes traffic to the SECONDARY until the primary recovers.

questions.question: A company uses RDS MySQL in a Multi-AZ deployment. During a maintenance window, the primary DB instance in us-east-1a fails. How long does the typical RDS Multi-AZ automatic failover take, and what is its impact on the connection string?
options: Failover takes 15-30 minutes; RDS publishes a CloudWatch event that triggers Lambda to push the new endpoint to the app
Failover is effectively instantaneous; RDS uses an internal load balancer that transparently redirects all connections
Failover takes 60-120 seconds; the endpoint CNAME automatically resolves to the new primary so no connection string change is needed
Failover takes 1-3 minutes; the application must update its connection string to point to the new primary endpoint
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ automatic failover typically takes 60-120 seconds. During failover, RDS updates the DNS CNAME of the DB endpoint to resolve to the standby instance (now promoted to primary). Applications using the endpoint hostname automatically reconnect to the new primary after the DNS TTL expires, without any configuration change.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer is setting up cross-region replication for S3 to support a disaster recovery strategy. The source bucket has existing objects that need to be replicated to the destination bucket. What steps are required to replicate the existing objects?
options: S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically replicates all existing objects when you enable the replication configuration
Open a case with AWS Support to request a one-time back-fill replication job for the existing objects in the bucket
Use S3 Batch Operations with a ReplicateObject job to back-fill the existing objects through the replication rules
Enable S3 Versioning on both buckets and then enable CRR — versioning automatically triggers back-fill replication
questions.explanation: S3 Cross-Region Replication only replicates objects written after the replication rule is enabled — pre-existing objects are not automatically replicated. To replicate existing objects, use S3 Batch Operations with the ReplicateObject operation, which processes existing objects and subjects them to the replication rules. This is the AWS-recommended approach for migrating existing data.

questions.question: A company's application uses a 3-tier architecture with an ALB, Auto Scaling group, and RDS. The application has an aggressive RTO of 5 minutes. Which DR approach is the ONLY feasible option?
options: Backup and restore using RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery in the DR region
Warm standby with pre-scaled instances that can take over production traffic within 5 minutes
Multi-site active-active deployment where both regions serve production traffic simultaneously
Pilot light with automated provisioning scripts that complete the full stack in under 5 minutes
questions.explanation: A 5-minute RTO is extremely aggressive. Only a multi-site active-active strategy reliably achieves it — both regions are already serving production traffic, so 'failover' is just adjusting Route 53 weights or removing the failed region's endpoint. Warm-standby scale-up can take minutes but may exceed 5 minutes. Pilot light and backup/restore both take 15+ minutes minimum.

questions.question: An application uses an Aurora MySQL cluster. During a major incident, the primary writer instance fails. The application continues to throw connection errors 10 minutes after the incident. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The application is caching the primary instance's IP address instead of resolving the cluster endpoint DNS name

Aurora Global Database cross-region failover is taking longer than the expected cluster endpoint propagation window — Global Database failover affects a secondary cluster in another region, not the primary instance promotion within the same cluster

The application's database connection pool exhausted all connections before the new primary instance was fully promoted in the cluster — connection pool exhaustion is a symptom, not the root cause; the cluster endpoint should redirect connections to the new primary instance automatically
Aurora read replicas do not automatically promote to the primary instance within the cluster, so manual operator intervention is required
questions.explanation: Aurora automatic failover typically completes in under 30 seconds — an existing read replica is promoted to primary. If errors persist 10 minutes later, the application is most likely caching a hardcoded IP for the old primary rather than resolving the cluster endpoint (a DNS CNAME) on each new connection. Always use the cluster endpoint DNS name.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to create an automated backup strategy for EC2 instances running a stateful application. Backups must occur daily, be retained for 30 days, and also be copied to a second AWS region. Which service provides this capability with the LEAST custom code?
options: A CloudFormation scheduled task that triggers an SSM Automation document to create EBS snapshots as a backup — this approach lacks centralised backup tracking, cross-region copy, and retention lifecycle management in a single backup plan
AWS Backup with a backup plan that defines daily frequency, 30-day retention, and a cross-region copy rule

A Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) policy that manages EBS snapshot backup schedules with a cross-region copy rule and a 30-day retention lifecycle — DLM handles EBS snapshots well but does not cover RDS, DynamoDB, or other services in a unified backup plan

A Lambda function triggered daily by EventBridge that creates EBS snapshots and copies them cross-region, deleting older backup copies after 30 days — functional but requires custom code to manage retention and lacks the centralised audit and compliance reporting of a managed backup plan
questions.explanation: AWS Backup is a fully managed backup service that supports EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, and more. A backup plan specifies the backup frequency, retention window, and lifecycle rules (Warm→Cold). Backup plans support cross-region copy rules natively, eliminating the need for custom Lambda code or manual snapshot management.

questions.question: A company requires that an EC2 Auto Scaling group maintains exactly 2 healthy instances at all times. When scale-out is triggered, a new instance must be verified with a custom health check before the old instance is terminated. How should the SysOps engineer implement this?
options: Configure lifecycle hooks on EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING and EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING to gate the custom health check before scaling actions complete

Set the ASG minimum to 2 and configure the ALB health check grace period so new instances are not marked unhealthy during scaling warm-up — this prevents premature termination but does not guarantee scripts complete before traffic arrives or before termination proceeds

Set the ASG health check type to ELB and configure the target group health check path to verify application readiness before the scaling event completes — health checks control traffic routing but do not pause the scaling lifecycle to allow scripts to finish

Use an ASG launch template with a custom user-data script that registers the instance with the load balancer only after the scaling initialisation completes — user-data runs before the instance is marked InService but cannot pause the scaling lifecycle hook for external service registration
questions.explanation: Lifecycle hooks let you insert custom actions during ASG scale-out (LAUNCHING) and scale-in (TERMINATING). During a rolling replacement, the LAUNCHING hook pauses the new instance in 'Pending:Wait' while your custom check validates it. Only after CompleteLifecycleAction does the instance enter InService. You coordinate this with the TERMINATING hook so capacity never drops below 2.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer notices that an ElastiCache Redis cluster is experiencing frequent cache misses during peak hours, causing high latency on the application. CloudWatch shows CPU at 40% and memory at 60%. What is the MOST likely issue?
options: The cache TTL values are set too short, so items expire before they can be reused during peak load and force refetch
The ElastiCache node type is undersized for the working set — upgrade to a memory-optimized instance type to handle peak load during high-traffic periods

The application is not using connection pooling, causing Redis cache connections to be created and destroyed for every request — connection exhaustion degrades performance but is a connection issue, not a cache hit ratio problem caused by TTL

Redis eviction policy is set to allkeys-lru, which removes cache items aggressively as memory fills, reducing the effective cache hit rate — eviction policy affects behaviour under memory pressure but does not explain low hit rate when cache TTL is too short
questions.explanation: When memory is at 60% and CPU is healthy, the most likely cause of cache misses at peak is excessive key eviction due to short TTL values. If keys expire quickly, data must be refetched from the database often. Review TTL settings on frequently accessed keys and inspect the 'Evictions' and 'CacheHits/CacheMisses' CloudWatch metrics for confirmation.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer deploys a CloudFormation stack but notices that the actual resources differ from the template definition — someone manually modified an EC2 security group directly in the console. Which CloudFormation feature detects this and what does it report?
options: CloudFormation rollback triggers detect out-of-band changes and automatically revert the actual resource configuration to match the previous stack state

CloudFormation Change Sets compare two template versions and highlight the actual differences before the change set is applied — Change Sets compare template A to template B, not the actual deployed resources against the template
An AWS Config CloudFormation-drift rule reports actual stack configuration changes when any resource deviates from the template
CloudFormation Stack Drift Detection, which compares actual resource configurations against the stack's expected template
questions.explanation: CloudFormation Drift Detection compares the current state of deployed resources against the expected state defined in the stack template. It reports which resources have drifted (been modified outside CloudFormation), identifies the specific property differences, and marks them as DRIFTED. This is distinct from Change Sets, which compare two template versions before deployment.

questions.question: An organization manages 500 EC2 instances across 10 AWS accounts. The security team requires that all instances have the SSM Agent installed and that OS patches are applied within 48 hours of release. Which approach provides the MOST scalable solution?
options: Configure each instance to pull and apply patches using cron jobs and a hand-rolled patching script per OS family
Create a Lambda function in each account that checks patch compliance and applies patches via SSM Run Command
Bake patches into AMIs monthly using EC2 Image Builder and replace all running instances during a maintenance window
Use AWS Organizations with Systems Manager Patch Manager and a maintenance window applied via SSM Quick Setup
questions.explanation: Systems Manager Patch Manager with SSM Quick Setup deploys a patch baseline and maintenance window configuration to all accounts in an AWS Organization at once. Fleet Manager provides cross-account visibility into patch compliance. This is the AWS-recommended approach for large-scale patching without per-account Lambda functions or custom scripts.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer uses CloudFormation StackSets to deploy an IAM role to all accounts in an AWS Organization. After the initial deployment, a new account joins the organization. How can the engineer ensure the IAM role is automatically deployed to the new account?
options: Re-run the StackSet deployment targeting all accounts so it includes the newly joined account — this requires manually triggering a re-deployment and does not automatically handle future accounts as they join
Enable 'Automatic Deployment' on the StackSet so new accounts joining the target OU receive the stack automatically

Manually deploy the stack to the newly joined account using the 'Add new stacks to accounts' option in the StackSet console — manual steps do not scale and do not automatically provision resources for accounts that join in the future

Create an EventBridge rule that detects new account creation events and triggers a Lambda function that automatically deploys a standalone CloudFormation stack to the new account — Lambda-based automation works but is more complex than using the native StackSet automatic deployment feature
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with AWS Organizations integration supports automatic deployment. When 'Automatic Deployment' is enabled, StackSets automatically deploys to new accounts as they join the target (OU or root). This eliminates manual intervention or custom automation whenever the organization structure changes.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to deploy a new application version to an Elastic Beanstalk environment with zero downtime. The deployment must keep the current instance count unchanged and roll back immediately if the new version has errors. Which deployment policy should be used?
options: Rolling with additional batch: maintains full capacity by launching extra instances and deploying in batches
Rolling: replaces instances in batches and temporarily reduces the available capacity during the deployment
All at once: deploys the new version to every instance simultaneously and accepts brief downtime during the update
Immutable: launches a fresh set of instances with the new version and swaps them in only after health checks pass
questions.explanation: Immutable deployment launches a completely new set of instances in a separate temporary ASG with the new application version. If health checks pass, the new instances are moved to the original ASG and old instances are terminated. If they fail, the temporary ASG is deleted with zero impact on the existing environment — true zero-downtime with instant rollback.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure consistent software configuration across 200 EC2 instances. If any instance's configuration drifts from the defined baseline (e.g., a configuration file is modified), it should be automatically remediated within 30 minutes. Which SSM feature implements this?
options: SSM State Manager with an association that applies an SSM document on a 30-minute schedule to enforce compliance
SSM Patch Manager with a custom compliance rule that checks configuration files instead of OS package versions
AWS Config with a custom rule that checks configuration files and triggers SSM Automation for remediation
SSM Run Command invoked by a scheduled EventBridge rule that fires every 30 minutes against the managed fleet
questions.explanation: SSM State Manager maintains a defined state for instances by running an SSM document on a schedule. The association can be configured to run every 30 minutes. If an instance's configuration drifts, the next scheduled run reapplies the desired configuration. This is the purpose-built feature for configuration compliance and drift remediation at scale.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to create a golden AMI that automatically incorporates the latest OS patches and installs specific packages every week. The resulting AMI should be distributed to three AWS regions. Which service provides this automated AMI build pipeline?
options: An SSM Automation document that launches an EC2 instance, installs packages, creates a snapshot, and registers a new AMI — this pipeline works but requires manual scheduling and does not provide native pipeline versioning, component reuse, or built-in cross-region distribution

AWS CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that runs Packer to build the AMI and distributes it to target regions — a functional image pipeline but introduces Packer as an external dependency and does not natively manage AMI lifecycle or compliance scanning
EC2 Image Builder with an image pipeline, recipe, and distribution settings that target the three regions

An AWS Lambda function triggered weekly by EventBridge to create an AMI from a running instance without a dedicated pipeline — creates AMIs from live instances rather than from a reproducible build pipeline, risking configuration drift
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder is a fully managed service for automated AMI creation. An image pipeline defines the schedule (weekly), an image recipe specifies the base AMI and components (update OS, install packages), and distribution settings list the target regions. Image Builder handles the instance launch, configuration, testing, and AMI creation automatically with no custom code.

questions.question: A CloudFormation stack update is attempted but fails midway. Some resources are successfully updated while others are not. The engineer needs to preview what resource changes will be made before executing another update. Which feature should be used?
options: AWS Config resource configuration history to see how each resource's actual configuration changed over time — Config shows configuration history but does not preview or show executing changes before a CloudFormation stack update is applied

CloudFormation Drift Detection to see what configuration changed from the expected template state — Drift Detection compares deployed resources to the current template; it does not preview changes before executing a new stack update
CloudFormation Change Sets to preview the proposed resource changes before executing the stack update

CloudFormation Stack Events to review which resources were updated in the previous deployment — Stack Events show past changes after executing a deployment, not a preview of proposed changes before executing
questions.explanation: CloudFormation Change Sets allow you to preview exactly which resources will be added, modified, or deleted before executing a stack update. After creating a change set from the new template, you review the proposed changes (resource action, physical ID, replacement status) and only execute when satisfied. This prevents unexpected modifications.

questions.question: A team has 50 EC2 instances in different accounts that need to run a custom shell script for emergency remediation. The script must run immediately with results reported centrally. Which SSM feature is best suited for this immediate one-time execution?
options: SSM Session Manager connecting to each instance individually so the engineer can run the command interactively — Session Manager works per instance and does not support running the same command across multiple instances in one operation
SSM Run Command targeting the instances by instance ID or tag, with command output sent to S3 or CloudWatch Logs

An SSM State Manager association configured with a once-run execution mode that targets all instances — State Manager associations are designed for continuous compliance, not ad-hoc one-shot commands across a specific set of instances

An SSM Automation document with an ExecuteScript action distributed to every instance in a loop — Automation documents are designed for multi-step workflows; Run Command is the simpler and more appropriate tool for running a single command across many instances
questions.explanation: SSM Run Command is designed for ad-hoc, immediate command execution on managed instances. You specify targets (instance IDs, tags, or resource groups), the SSM document or shell script to run, and configure output to CloudWatch Logs or S3 for centralized reporting. It supports cross-account targeting when instances have the correct IAM roles.

questions.question: A Service Catalog product based on a CloudFormation template needs to be updated to use a newer AMI ID. The constraint is that developers using the product should not be able to modify the AMI ID parameter when provisioning. How should the SysOps engineer configure this?
options: Publish a new Service Catalog product version with the updated template, plus a Template Constraint pinning the AMI ID

Use a Launch Constraint with an IAM role that only permits the product to launch the original catalog template version — Launch Constraints restrict permissions but do not enforce a specific product version or notify existing provisioned-product owners about catalog updates

Add an AWS Config rule that terminates any EC2 instance launched from an unapproved catalog AMI version — Config can detect non-compliant resources but cannot roll back existing provisioned products to an updated catalog version

Update the CloudFormation template directly so all provisioned products automatically inherit the updated changes without re-provisioning — provisioned products are not automatically updated when the underlying template changes; a new catalog version must be published and applied
questions.explanation: Service Catalog Template Constraints let administrators restrict the values users can enter for CloudFormation parameters at provisioning time. By specifying allowed values or pinning the AMI ID parameter, you prevent users from overriding it with unapproved AMIs. Publishing a new product version with the updated template provides the upgrade path.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to verify that all EC2 instances in a fleet are running the latest approved AMI from the organization's image catalog. Non-compliant instances should be reported and optionally replaced automatically. Which solution addresses this most effectively?
options: Tag every EC2 instance with its AMI ID and use the Tag Editor to identify the instances that are not compliant with approved AMI IDs — tagging and Tag Editor provide visibility but do not evaluate compliance automatically or trigger remediation for non-compliant instances
AWS Config managed rule 'approved-amis-by-id' with auto-remediation through SSM Automation to replace non-compliant instances
Enable GuardDuty EC2 instance profiling, which detects instances launched from unapproved or untrusted AMIs in real time

Write a Lambda function that describes all EC2 instances and compares their AMI IDs against the compliant approved list, emailing a non-compliance report — a custom Lambda can detect non-compliant instances but requires manual scheduling and does not integrate with AWS Config's continuous evaluation and auto-remediation
questions.explanation: AWS Config managed rule 'approved-amis-by-id' (or 'approved-amis-by-tag') evaluates EC2 instances against an approved AMI list. Non-compliant instances are flagged in the Config compliance dashboard. Config auto-remediation can trigger an SSM Automation document that replaces the instance. This provides continuous compliance evaluation without custom Lambda code.

questions.question: GuardDuty generates a finding type 'UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/SSHBruteForce' for an EC2 instance. The SysOps engineer needs to automatically block the source IP addresses identified in the finding. What is the MOST automated approach?
options: Configure an EventBridge rule that triggers a Lambda to extract the source IP and add it to a WAF IP set or NACL deny rule
Enable GuardDuty automated remediation, which natively blocks the source IPs identified in each finding it raises
Use AWS Security Hub to route the finding to a SIEM that blocks the IP via integration with network devices
Manually review the GuardDuty finding and add the source IP to a security group's deny rules in the console
questions.explanation: GuardDuty itself does not block traffic — it generates findings. The recommended automated remediation pattern uses EventBridge: create a rule matching the GuardDuty finding type, trigger a Lambda function that parses the finding for the attacker IP, then update a Network ACL deny rule or a WAF IP set. This provides near-real-time automated threat response.

questions.question: A company uses AWS Organizations with 15 member accounts. The security team wants to prevent any account from disabling CloudTrail or modifying CloudTrail logs. Which control provides the strongest enforcement?
options: Enable AWS Config managed rule 'cloud-trail-enabled' across every account with a remediation action — Config can detect when CloudTrail is disabled but does not preventively control the ability to stop logging; an SCP is needed to deny the API call
Apply a Service Control Policy at the organization root that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, DeleteTrail, and UpdateTrail

Configure CloudTrail with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode on the destination bucket — Object Lock prevents deletion of log files already delivered but does not control or prevent stopping the CloudTrail trail itself

Create an IAM permission boundary in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging — permission boundaries constrain identity-based policies within an account but can be overridden by account administrators; an SCP provides organization-wide control that cannot be bypassed
questions.explanation: Service Control Policies applied at the Organizations root or OU level override IAM permissions in member accounts — even account administrators cannot perform denied actions. An SCP denying cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and cloudtrail:UpdateTrail prevents any identity in member accounts from disabling CloudTrail. IAM permission boundaries apply only to IAM entities, not the root user.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to assess EC2 instances for known CVEs, CIS benchmark compliance, and network exposure findings. The findings should be prioritized by severity and associated with specific package versions. Which AWS service provides this?
options: AWS GuardDuty EC2 instance profiling for vulnerability scanning of running instances to surface CVEs — GuardDuty performs threat detection using logs and network traffic, not vulnerability scanning against CVEs; it does not scan OS packages for known vulnerabilities
AWS Inspector v2 with EC2 scanning enabled, which continuously surfaces CVEs and network reachability findings

AWS Config with the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark conformance pack evaluating instances against CVEs and patch compliance — Config checks configuration compliance, not software vulnerability CVEs; it does not perform OS-level package scanning

AWS Security Hub configured with a third-party vulnerability scanner integration to surface CVEs across all EC2 instances — Security Hub aggregates findings from integrated tools but is not itself a vulnerability scanner; Inspector v2 natively surfaces CVEs
questions.explanation: AWS Inspector v2 provides automated vulnerability management for EC2 instances. It continuously scans for CVEs using the SSM Agent, reports findings with CVE identifiers, affected package versions, and CVSS severity scores. It also performs network reachability analysis to identify exposed ports. Inspector requires the SSM Agent and uses Systems Manager for scanning without deploying additional agents.

questions.question: A company stores sensitive customer data in S3 buckets across multiple accounts. The security team wants a single view of all security findings, compliance status, and Inspector results across all accounts. Which service provides this aggregated security posture view?
options: AWS Organizations Trusted Advisor cross-account dashboard aggregating security alerts from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie across all accounts — Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks, not a unified cross-account security finding aggregator; Inspector findings are not surfaced in Trusted Advisor
AWS Security Hub with cross-account aggregation and the GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and Config integrations enabled

An AWS Config aggregator showing compliance status across every account and region — Config aggregators show resource compliance against Config rules; they do not aggregate GuardDuty threats, Inspector vulnerability findings, or Macie data-classification alerts in one view

CloudTrail Lake configured for cross-account security event analysis with a federated query interface — CloudTrail Lake aggregates API activity logs; it does not surface GuardDuty alerts, Inspector findings, or Macie classifications
questions.explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates findings from multiple AWS security services (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, IAM Access Analyzer, Firewall Manager) across multiple accounts and regions into a single normalized view. It applies security standards (CIS AWS Foundations, AWS FSBP) and calculates a security score. Cross-account aggregation requires enabling Security Hub in a designated administrator account.

questions.question: A company's compliance requirement mandates that all KMS customer-managed keys must be rotated at least once per year. A SysOps engineer needs to enforce this automatically. What is the SIMPLEST method?
options: Set up AWS Config rule 'cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled' to detect customer-managed KMS keys that have not been rotated within the past year and alert the security team — Config can detect non-compliance but does not automatically rotate customer keys; only the native automatic rotation setting does that

Create an EventBridge scheduled rule that triggers a Lambda function to rotate all customer-managed KMS keys by creating a new key alias every year — Lambda can create new keys but cannot rotate the backing key material of an existing customer key; only the built-in KMS rotation does so transparently

Use the KMS API to create a new key version for every customer-managed key annually and update every application's key reference — KMS does not support explicit key versions that applications can reference; re-encrypting all data with a new customer key annually is operationally complex and not necessary when automatic rotation handles backing-key material rotation each year
Enable automatic key rotation on each customer-managed KMS key, which rotates the backing key material every year
questions.explanation: KMS supports automatic annual key rotation for symmetric customer-managed keys. When enabled, KMS automatically rotates the backing key material every 365 days. The key ID, ARN, and alias remain unchanged — all encrypted data can still be decrypted without any application changes since KMS retains all previous backing key versions. This is the simplest zero-effort rotation.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to identify all S3 buckets in a specific AWS account that may contain personally identifiable information (PII) such as social security numbers or credit card numbers. Which service should the engineer use?
options: AWS GuardDuty S3 protection, which detects PII by analyzing S3 data access patterns and API calls across all buckets — GuardDuty S3 protection detects malicious access and policy anomalies, not PII classification within S3 buckets

Amazon Comprehend medical or PII detection triggered by a Lambda function on each new S3 object upload across all buckets — Comprehend can detect PII in individual objects, but running it on every upload across all buckets requires custom Lambda orchestration and does not provide automatic discovery of existing objects
AWS Macie, which uses machine learning to automatically discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in S3 buckets

AWS Config combined with S3 server access logging to detect PII appearing in the object key names stored in buckets — S3 access logs record API calls and object key names, not the object content; they cannot identify PII stored inside objects in buckets
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie is specifically designed for automated sensitive-data discovery and classification in S3. It uses machine learning to identify sensitive data types including PII (names, SSNs, credit card numbers, email addresses), financial information, and healthcare data. Macie generates findings that identify the affected S3 objects and data types. GuardDuty analyzes access patterns but does not inspect content.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to verify that no S3 bucket in the account is publicly accessible. The check should be continuous and run whenever a new bucket is created. Which solution has the LOWEST operational overhead?
options: Create an EventBridge rule on CreateBucket API calls that triggers a Lambda to check and apply the Block Public Access setting to each new bucket at the account level — this reactive approach leaves a window between bucket creation and the Lambda execution during which the bucket may be public

Apply an SCP denying s3:PutBucketAcl API calls that include public-read or public-read-write grants at the account level — SCPs can restrict public ACL changes but cannot retroactively block public access on buckets where it was already enabled before the SCP was applied

Use AWS Config managed rule 's3-bucket-public-read-prohibited' to detect non-compliant buckets and automatically remediate them at the account level via SSM — Config evaluates compliance and can trigger remediation but does not prevent public access as effectively as enabling Block Public Access at the account level
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level, which applies to all existing and future buckets automatically
questions.explanation: S3 Block Public Access at the account level is a single toggle that prevents any bucket in the account from being made public — it overrides bucket policies and ACLs that would grant public access. It applies to all existing and future buckets. This is the lowest-overhead preventive control, requiring no Config rules, Lambda functions, or SCPs to maintain.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer uses IAM Access Analyzer. It reports that an IAM role in the account has a trust policy that allows cross-account access from an external AWS account that the company does not recognize. What should the engineer do FIRST?
options: Review the IAM Access Analyzer finding details to determine whether the access is intentional, then archive or revoke

Delete the IAM role immediately to prevent any further unauthorized cross-account access — deleting the role without reviewing the IAM Access Analyzer finding details and understanding the intended use risks disrupting legitimate business workflows

Open a case with AWS Support to identify the owner of the external AWS account that the IAM Access Analyzer flagged — AWS Support cannot disclose information about external accounts; the finding details in IAM Access Analyzer should be reviewed first to determine whether the access is intentional

Enable GuardDuty to monitor API calls made by the external account's assumed-role sessions — GuardDuty detects threats in real-time but does not help determine whether an existing IAM Access Analyzer finding represents an intended or unintended cross-account trust
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resource-based policies (IAM roles, S3 buckets, KMS keys, etc.) that grant access to external principals outside your zone of trust. The first step is to review the finding details — sometimes cross-account trusts are intentional (vendor integrations, MSPs). You should archive intentional access and revoke or fix unintended access by modifying the trust policy.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to verify that a CloudTrail log file delivered to S3 has not been tampered with since it was created. Which CloudTrail feature enables this verification?
options: CloudTrail's CloudWatch Logs integration, which stores log events in CloudWatch so any modification after being delivered to S3 can be detected by a CloudWatch alarm — CloudWatch Logs stores a copy of events but does not cryptographically prove that the original S3 log file was tampered with after being delivered

CloudTrail log file encryption with KMS, which ensures that the logs cannot be modified or decrypted without the KMS key after being delivered — KMS encryption protects confidentiality but does not detect whether a log file was deleted or modified after it was delivered
CloudTrail log file integrity validation, which writes a signed digest with SHA-256 hashes of every delivered log file

S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the trail bucket, which prevents log file deletion or overwriting after being delivered — Object Lock prevents tampering prospectively but does not cryptographically validate the integrity of a log file that has already been delivered
questions.explanation: CloudTrail log file integrity validation creates a digitally signed digest file every hour that contains SHA-256 hashes of all log files delivered in that period. You can use the 'aws cloudtrail validate-logs' CLI command to verify whether any log files have been modified, deleted, or tampered with. The digest files themselves are signed with a private key owned by CloudTrail.

questions.question: A web application behind an Application Load Balancer is receiving automated bot attacks that generate 1000+ requests per second from a single IP address. The legitimate user base comes from North America and Europe only. Which AWS WAF configuration best mitigates this?
options: Create a Network ACL deny entry for the attacking IP address on every public-facing subnet — NACLs can block individual IPs but do not rate-limit requests or automatically update to handle rotating attack IP addresses

Configure AWS Shield Advanced with DDoS protection to automatically block all attack requests at the network layer — Shield Advanced protects against volumetric DDoS attacks at the infrastructure layer but does not apply application-layer rate limiting per IP for HTTP requests

Enable the AWS WAF managed rule group 'AWS-AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList' to block requests from known malicious IPs — IP reputation rules block known bad sources but do not limit the rate of requests from legitimate or new IP addresses that may be part of the attack
Create a WAF rate-based rule limiting 1000 requests per 5-minute window per IP, combined with a geo-match rule blocking non-NA/EU
questions.explanation: A rate-based rule (1000 req/5 min threshold) automatically blocks individual IPs exceeding the rate limit — this directly addresses the bot pattern. A geographic match rule restricting traffic to North America and Europe reduces the attack surface from global bot networks. Together they provide layered protection. NACLs require manual IP updates, and Shield Advanced focuses on volumetric DDoS at the network layer.

questions.question: A company has two VPCs in the same AWS region: VPC-A (10.0.0.0/16) and VPC-B (172.16.0.0/16). Resources in both VPCs need to communicate privately. The SysOps engineer sets up VPC peering. After creation, instances in VPC-A still cannot reach instances in VPC-B. What is MOST likely missing?
options: VPC peering requires an Internet Gateway in each VPC to function, even for fully private CIDR communication
VPC peering requires both VPCs to be in the same AWS account, otherwise traffic between them is not permitted
Route table entries have not been added in each VPC to direct traffic for the peer's CIDR to the peering connection
Security groups in both VPCs must explicitly allow all inter-VPC traffic, regardless of routing configuration
questions.explanation: VPC peering establishes the connection but traffic will not flow until route table entries are added. In VPC-A's route table you must add a route for 172.16.0.0/16 via the peering connection ID (pcx-xxx). In VPC-B's route table you must add a route for 10.0.0.0/16 via the same peering connection. Security groups must also allow the traffic, but missing routes is the #1 cause of failed peering.

questions.question: A company has 10 VPCs that all need to communicate with each other and share access to a central services VPC (monitoring, DNS, security scanning). VPC peering would require 45 peering connections. What is the recommended solution?
options: Create a hub-and-spoke VPC peering topology with the central services VPC acting as the hub for all spokes
Use AWS Transit Gateway to enable transitive routing between all VPCs through a single managed hub attachment
Use VPC sharing via AWS Resource Access Manager to merge all VPCs into one shared network namespace
Create a VPN mesh between all VPCs using EC2-based VPN appliances to handle the cross-VPC routing fabric
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a hub that enables transitive routing between all attached VPCs with a single attachment per VPC instead of N×(N-1)/2 peering connections. With 10 VPCs plus 1 central services VPC, you create 11 Transit Gateway attachments. Route tables on the TGW control which VPCs can communicate. Transit Gateway also supports VPN and Direct Connect attachments.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer is troubleshooting why a private EC2 instance in a private subnet cannot access the internet to download packages during bootstrap. The instance has a valid security group rule allowing all outbound traffic. What should the engineer check first?
options: Verify that the Network ACL on the private subnet allows outbound traffic on port 443 to the wider internet
Verify that the private subnet's route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 default route pointing to a NAT Gateway in a public subnet
Verify that the Internet Gateway is attached to the VPC and reachable from the route table associated with the subnet
Verify that the EC2 instance has a public IP address assigned and is therefore routable from the public internet
questions.explanation: Private subnet instances do not have public IPs and use a NAT Gateway for outbound internet access. The private subnet's route table must have a route 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway ID. The NAT Gateway must be in a public subnet whose route table has 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway. A missing route in the private subnet's table is the most common cause.

questions.question: An application requires low-latency, highly available internet-facing access to UDP-based traffic on port 53 (DNS) and TCP port 443. Which AWS load balancer should the SysOps engineer deploy?
options: Classic Load Balancer with TCP listeners on port 53 and port 443 attached to the registered target instances
Application Load Balancer (ALB) with listener rules configured for both port 53 UDP and port 443 HTTPS traffic
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) configured for transparent traffic inspection on all ports including UDP and TCP
Network Load Balancer (NLB), which operates at Layer 4 and supports TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, and TLS listener protocols
questions.explanation: Network Load Balancers operate at Layer 4 and support TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, and TLS listeners. NLB handles millions of requests per second at ultra-low latency. For UDP port 53 traffic, NLB is the only AWS load balancer option (ALB supports HTTP/HTTPS only). NLB also supports static Elastic IPs per Availability Zone, useful for DNS services that require stable IPs.

questions.question: A company's website is distributed globally via CloudFront. The origin is an ALB in us-east-1. Users in Asia are experiencing slow first-byte times for dynamic content that cannot be cached. How can CloudFront reduce latency for these dynamic requests?
options: Use a CloudFront Origin Request Policy that compresses dynamic content responses returned for requests — compression reduces payload size but does not reduce the number of requests reaching the origin or the volume of redundant content fetched from the ALB

Configure the CloudFront distribution with a custom SSL certificate to reduce TLS overhead for content requests — a custom certificate reduces certificate negotiation differences but does not reduce the number of origin content requests or cache consolidation for the ALB

Create new CloudFront edge locations in Asia by purchasing dedicated CloudFront capacity reservations to serve content requests closer to users — dedicated edge capacity improves latency but does not reduce the number of redundant content requests forwarded to the ALB origin
Enable CloudFront Origin Shield in the AWS region closest to the ALB to consolidate origin requests for dynamic content
questions.explanation: CloudFront Origin Shield is an additional caching layer in a specific AWS region between edge locations and the origin. For dynamic content that cannot be cached, Origin Shield still benefits performance by routing traffic through the AWS backbone network (rather than the public internet) from the edge location to the origin. This reduces RTT and network jitter for users far from the origin region.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to give a third-party auditor application running in the auditor's AWS account access to read-only CloudWatch metrics from the company's AWS account. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: Create a cross-account IAM role in the company's account with a trust on the auditor's account and read-only CloudWatch permissions
Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability and use the auditor's monitoring account to pull metrics from the source
Create an IAM user in the company's account with read-only CloudWatch permissions and share the access keys with the auditor
Share the company's AWS console credentials with the auditor on a temporary basis for the duration of the audit window
questions.explanation: Cross-account IAM roles are the AWS best practice for granting external accounts access. The role in the company's account has a trust policy specifying the auditor's account ID as a trusted principal. The auditor's application calls sts:AssumeRole to obtain temporary credentials scoped to read-only CloudWatch access. No long-lived credentials are shared, and access is revocable at any time.

questions.question: A company connects its on-premises data center to AWS using AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Users report intermittent connectivity failures to the VPN. The SysOps engineer checks and finds the VPN has only one tunnel active. What should the engineer do to improve availability?
options: Add a second Internet Gateway to the VPC to provide additional active redundancy for the on-premises VPN connection — Internet Gateways provide internet connectivity, not VPN tunnel redundancy; AWS Site-to-Site VPN supports two tunnels per connection for active redundancy
Ensure both VPN tunnels are configured and active on the customer gateway, with BGP or static routes for both tunnel IPs

Upgrade from static routing to BGP routing on the existing single-tunnel VPN connection to enable active failover — BGP improves routing flexibility but a single active tunnel still means no redundancy; both tunnels must be active for HA

Create an additional Site-to-Site VPN connection to a different Virtual Private Gateway endpoint — creating a second VPN connection is more complex than enabling the already-available second tunnel on the existing connection to achieve active redundancy
questions.explanation: Each AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection provides two tunnels for redundancy — each tunnel connects to a different endpoint in a different AWS Availability Zone. Many customer gateway devices only bring up one tunnel. The correct fix is to configure both tunnel endpoints on the customer gateway device, enable both tunnels, and configure routing (BGP preferred) to use both. AWS then maintains HA within the VPN connection.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to securely access EC2 instances in a private subnet for administration without opening inbound SSH or RDP ports and without requiring a bastion host. Which AWS service enables this?
options: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, which uses the SSM Agent and outbound HTTPS to open browser or CLI sessions
An EC2 VPC Endpoint that allows direct private connectivity to instance consoles over the AWS PrivateLink network
AWS Direct Connect to establish a private connection from the administrator's workstation into the VPC subnet
EC2 Instance Connect configured with an Internet Gateway route attached to the private subnet for inbound SSH
questions.explanation: SSM Session Manager provides interactive shell access to EC2 instances via the SSM Agent, which makes an outbound HTTPS connection to the SSM endpoint. No inbound security group rules or open ports are required. Sessions are logged to CloudWatch Logs or S3 for audit. Session Manager supports both Linux (bash) and Windows (PowerShell) and eliminates the bastion host operational overhead.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer needs to expose an internal application running on EC2 instances to other AWS accounts without VPC peering or Transit Gateway. The solution must not expose the service to the internet. Which AWS service enables this?
options: AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) exposing the service via an NLB so consumer accounts can create interface endpoints
VPC sharing through AWS Resource Access Manager to share subnets across the consumer accounts in the organization
AWS Direct Connect cross-connect to link the two AWS accounts together at the physical Layer-1 transport network
S3 presigned URL-based file sharing between the producer and consumer accounts handled through the service team
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) lets you expose a service backed by an NLB in your VPC to other VPCs or accounts through Interface VPC Endpoints. Consumer accounts create an interface endpoint that gets a private IP in their VPC. Traffic never leaves the AWS network, and you don't need VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or internet exposure. You control which accounts can create endpoints via the service allow-list.

questions.question: An application uses AWS Direct Connect for production traffic. The company wants to ensure that if the Direct Connect connection fails, traffic automatically fails over to a Site-to-Site VPN. What is the AWS-recommended architecture for this?
options: Use Route 53 health checks to detect Direct Connect failure and reroute traffic to another site — Route 53 health checks operate at the DNS level; they do not automatically switch the network path from Direct Connect to a backup Site-to-Site VPN
Configure a Site-to-Site VPN on the same Virtual Private Gateway as the Direct Connect, with BGP preferring DX over VPN

Enable Direct Connect resilience recommendations in the Direct Connect console and add a second physical connection — a second Direct Connect connection is the highest resilience option but is expensive; a Site-to-Site VPN on the same Virtual Private Gateway is the standard cost-effective backup for a single site

Create two Direct Connect connections in an active-standby configuration for the same site — dual Direct Connect connections are costly; a Site-to-Site VPN provides sufficient backup connectivity for a single on-premises site without the expense of a second leased line
questions.explanation: AWS recommends configuring a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup for Direct Connect using the same Virtual Private Gateway. With BGP, the Direct Connect route is preferred over the VPN route (lower MED / higher local preference). When Direct Connect fails, BGP withdraws those routes and traffic automatically flows over the VPN. This is the standard hybrid-connectivity resilience pattern.

questions.question: A CloudFront distribution is serving static content from an S3 bucket. The security team requires that only CloudFront can access the S3 bucket directly — the bucket itself should not be publicly accessible. How should this be configured?
options: Create a CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) and update the S3 bucket policy to only allow the OAC service principal
Configure the CloudFront distribution to issue signed URLs and configure the S3 bucket to require signed requests
Set the S3 bucket policy to allow all CloudFront IP address ranges published in the AWS IP-ranges JSON document
Enable S3 Block Public Access and configure CloudFront to forward authentication headers from viewers to the origin
questions.explanation: CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) — the modern replacement for Origin Access Identity (OAI) — secures the S3 origin by allowing only the CloudFront distribution to make requests. The S3 bucket policy grants access to the CloudFront OAC service principal (cloudfront.amazonaws.com) with a condition on the distribution's ARN. The bucket itself stays private with public access blocked.

questions.question: A company runs 20 EC2 instances that process workloads 24/7 for the next 3 years. The current on-demand spend is $8,000/month. Which pricing model provides the GREATEST discount for this predictable, steady-state workload?
options: Convertible Reserved Instances for a 3-year term, providing up to 66% discount with flexibility to change families
Compute Savings Plans for flexibility across instance families and regions with up to 66% discount over on-demand
Spot Instances for the highest discount of up to 90%, accepting occasional interruptions during the 3-year horizon
Standard Reserved Instances for a 3-year all-upfront term, providing up to 72% discount for the fixed shape
questions.explanation: Standard Reserved Instances with a 3-year all-upfront payment provide the maximum discount (up to 72%) for EC2. They are locked to a specific instance type, size, region, and OS. For workloads with absolutely known, fixed requirements for 3 years, this is the most cost-effective option. Compute Savings Plans offer ~66% with more flexibility; Convertible RIs offer ~66% with instance-family flexibility.

questions.question: A data processing application needs to run batch jobs for 6 hours daily. The jobs are stateless and checkpointing is implemented so they can restart from the last checkpoint. Which EC2 pricing model minimizes cost for this workload?
options: Dedicated Hosts for exclusive hardware access and predictable per-instance pricing on the dedicated server
On-demand instances to guarantee availability of capacity for the 6-hour daily processing window each day
Spot Instances, which provide up to 90% discount and support graceful interruption via the 2-minute notice
Reserved Instances for 1 year with partial-upfront payment to cover the scheduled batch processing window
questions.explanation: Spot Instances are ideal for fault-tolerant batch workloads that implement checkpointing. AWS provides a 2-minute interruption notice via instance metadata and CloudWatch Events, allowing the application to save its checkpoint and gracefully terminate. The job restarts from the checkpoint on a new Spot Instance, achieving up to 90% cost savings versus on-demand. Checkpointing is the key enabler for Spot on batch jobs.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer is reviewing S3 storage costs and finds that a bucket stores 100 TB of objects. Most objects are accessed frequently for the first 30 days and rarely thereafter. After 1 year, objects are almost never accessed but must be retained for 7 years. Which S3 lifecycle configuration minimizes storage costs?
options: Transition to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year, expiring at the 7-year mark
Keep everything in S3 Standard for simplicity and enable versioning to guard against any accidental deletions
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which automatically moves objects to the lowest-cost tier regardless of object size
Transition to S3 One Zone-IA after 30 days for maximum cost savings and delete the objects at the 7-year mark
questions.explanation: A lifecycle policy transitioning to Standard-IA after 30 days (60-70% cheaper than Standard) and Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year (80-90% cheaper than Standard) matches the access pattern at minimal cost. Intelligent-Tiering also works but adds a per-object monitoring charge that may not pay off for large objects with predictable access. One Zone-IA lacks the redundancy needed for long-term retention.

questions.question: A company's monthly AWS bill has increased by $15,000 unexpectedly. The SysOps engineer needs to identify the root cause. Cost Explorer shows the increase is in the EC2 service. Which AWS tool automatically detects cost anomalies and sends an alert when spending deviates from expected patterns?
options: AWS Budgets with a monthly cost alert threshold configured to the expected dollar amount — Budgets alert when spending exceeds a threshold but do not identify the root cause of the increase or pinpoint which service or linked account caused the anomaly

Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks that flag services exceeding the budget threshold and provide root cost recommendations — Trusted Advisor identifies general cost savings opportunities but does not perform anomaly detection or surface the specific root cause of an unexpected spend spike
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, which uses machine learning to detect unusual spend and surface root-cause analysis

A CloudWatch billing alarm on the EstimatedCharges metric with an absolute threshold — the alarm fires when total charges exceed the set threshold but does not perform machine learning anomaly detection or identify the root cause of cost increases
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn your historical spend patterns and alerts you when spending deviates anomalously — even when the increase stays within a static budget. Unlike Budgets, it detects relative anomalies without needing a specific threshold. It provides root-cause analysis (which service/account/region/tag drove the anomaly) and delivers alerts via SNS or email.

questions.question: AWS Trusted Advisor reports that an account has 15 EC2 instances with very low CPU utilization (average < 5%) over the past 2 weeks. The SysOps engineer needs to provide right-sizing recommendations with specific instance type suggestions. Which AWS service provides detailed right-sizing recommendations based on CloudWatch metric analysis?
options: CloudWatch detailed monitoring dashboards combined with manual analysis to derive the optimal instance type — dashboards visualise metrics but require a human to interpret the data and do not automatically recommend a right-sized instance type

AWS Cost Explorer right-sizing recommendations surfaced in the dedicated recommendations tab — Cost Explorer right-sizing analyses cost and usage data for EC2 instances; it is less granular than Compute Optimizer, which analyses actual CloudWatch CPU, memory, network, and disk metrics per instance
AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes CloudWatch CPU, memory, network, and disk metrics and recommends instance types

AWS Trusted Advisor, which provides right-sizing recommendations in its cost optimisation checks — Trusted Advisor surfaces basic right-sizing hints for underutilised EC2 instances based on CPU utilisation alone, not the full multi-metric instance-level analysis provided by Compute Optimizer
questions.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2 instance configuration and CloudWatch utilization metrics (CPU, memory with the CloudWatch agent, network I/O, disk I/O) and provides specific right-sizing recommendations including the recommended instance type, projected CPU and memory utilization after the change, and estimated cost savings. It also supports Auto Scaling groups, EBS volumes, Lambda functions, and ECS/Fargate tasks.

questions.question: A SysOps engineer is reviewing a monthly AWS bill and notices that data transfer costs between two EC2 instances have increased significantly. The instances are in different Availability Zones within the same region. How can the engineer reduce these data transfer costs?
options: Move the two EC2 instances to the same Availability Zone in order to eliminate the inter-AZ data transfer fees
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to route traffic between the two instances instead of direct EC2 communication
Purchase an AWS Data Transfer Savings Plan to reduce per-GB inter-AZ data transfer costs for these instances
Use VPC Peering between the two Availability Zones to eliminate the inter-AZ data transfer costs entirely
questions.explanation: Inter-AZ data transfer within the same AWS region incurs a charge of $0.01/GB in each direction. Moving frequently communicating instances to the same Availability Zone eliminates these charges entirely. The tradeoff is reduced availability (both instances in one AZ). For architectures where cost outweighs multi-AZ redundancy for non-critical components, co-locating instances in the same AZ significantly reduces transfer costs.

questions.question: A company runs an RDS database that processes heavy read traffic during business hours and minimal traffic at night. The database currently uses a db.r5.2xlarge instance. Which cost optimization approach should the SysOps engineer recommend for the read traffic?
options: Add RDS Read Replicas to offload read traffic and scale them down off-peak — or use Aurora Auto Scaling for read replicas
Enable RDS Multi-AZ to distribute the read traffic across the primary and the standby instance during peak hours
Switch to a larger RDS instance type to handle the peak read traffic more efficiently and absorb traffic spikes
Enable RDS Proxy to pool the database connections and reduce primary instance load during traffic peaks
questions.explanation: RDS Read Replicas offload read-heavy traffic from the primary instance, reducing its load and allowing horizontal scaling during peak hours. With Aurora, Aurora Auto Scaling can automatically add and remove read replicas based on CPU or connections metrics, providing elastic capacity that scales down during off-peak hours. This avoids paying for a permanently oversized primary instance. Multi-AZ standby does not serve read traffic.
